title: Runway sweep — personal prep scratchpad
content:
Context: quick, noisy personal checklist for the weekly Runway Sweep (release train) meeting. This is my handheld list for the 1:1s and for dialing in owners during the sync. Not formal — things I need to confirm out loud and note who will own follow-ups.

Meeting: Runway Sweep — Weekly Release Readiness
When: Thu 09:00 PT (30m) — prep window 08:30–09:00 for owners
Attendees (expected): release captains, infra oncall, SRE lead, product PM, QA lead, build/release eng

Top objective: surface any showstopper risks and confirm go/no-go gating status for current train (v2026.03). If any hard blocker, define rollback or mitigation and owner.

My quick agenda (for me to follow):
- 0–5m: Quick heartbeat — are any teams calling immediate blockers? (ask each captain)
- 5–12m: Build & deploy health — artifacts, image promotions, infra migrations, DB migrations
- 12–20m: QA & smoke results — passing rates on canary slices, critical test failures, flakiness spikes
- 20–25m: SLO/observability — dashboards, error budget burn, ingestion/backfill risks
- 25–30m: Decision + owners for next 24h actions (who's on hot list)

Runway sweep personal checklist (speak these out loud):
1) Build artifacts promoted? Owner: Samir — status: need SHA for canary image (confirm tag present in registry). Timebox 10m.
2) DB migration blockers? Owner: Rowan — confirm dry-run completed and migration window locked. If migration fails in dry-run -> delay train.
3) Canary slice traffic routing verified? Owner: SRE oncall — ensure 1% traffic routed, latency within baseline. If p95 > baseline + 50ms => escalate.
4) Feature flags toggles and kill switches in place? Owner: PM (TBD) — make sure FF gates for risky features are ready to be closed instantly.
5) Critical automated tests: smoke + auth flow + payments flow are green on canary. Owner: QA lead — confirm green + test durations. Any flaky test -> mark as replaced by manual sanity.
6) Observability probes: tracing, errors, metric ingestion all OK? Owner: observability (Jon) — no recent schema changes.
7) Rollout window + oncall rotations confirmed? Owner: release captain — list 1st/2nd oncall for next 72h.
8) Backfill / batch jobs scheduled and isolated? Owner: infra-batch — ensure low-priority queues and throttles set.

Go / No-go gating criteria (my shorthand):
- Hard No-go if: build artifact missing OR DB migration dry-run failed OR canary shows critical error rate spike (>0.5% user-impacting errors) OR security finding blocking release.
- Conditional Go if: minor flaky tests or small telemetry regressions that are under threshold and have mitigations + owner + rollback plan.
- Soft Go (canary first): If non-critical regressions, proceed with canary rollout with immediate rollback path.

Rollback decision ladder (to speak during meeting):
- If canary shows regression: pause traffic -> roll image back to previous SHA -> notify prod-sRE Slack channel and start incident triage.
- If DB migration fails mid-run: stop deploys, revert DB migration if reversible, open incident ticket and escalate to schema owners.

Immediate tasks I must own/follow up after meeting: (tick off during meeting)
- [ ] Confirm registry tag for canary (Samir) — ping in thread, add tag to release notes.
- [ ] Validate migration dry-run logs (Rowan) — ask for link and quick summary in chat.
- [ ] Request smoke test artifact list and durations (QA) — mark flaky tests and capture ticket IDs.
- [ ] Verify that FF kill switches are documented in riot doc (PM) — if not, request one-liner with rollback toggle.
- [ ] Ensure oncall roster posted to ops-runbook (Captain) — screenshot link.

Notes to self / talking points:
- Ask: "Are there any infra change windows overlapping with the rollout?" (we had a storage controller refresh scheduled last month; double-check)
- Call out: yesterday's transient auth flake — did we root cause? If not, require guardrail: reduce traffic to 0.5% canary until follow-up.
- If any team says "we're good" but cannot show logs/dashboards: push for evidence (link + one screenshot).

Risks I'm keeping an eye on (ranked quick):
- 1 (high): DB migration ambiguous backward compatibility change (shortest mitigation: hold train until migration contract clarified)
- 2 (med): Observability ingest lag causing blind spots during rollout (mitigation: extra logging, longer initial watch window)
- 3 (low): Non-blocking flaky tests accidentally merged — track by replacing with guard test and escalate to QA.

Preemptive escalation chain (short):
- 1st: Release captain (Slack @release-captain)
- 2nd: SRE lead (Slack @sre-lead)
- 3rd: Eng director oncall if >30m unresolved blocker (phone)

Post-meeting follow-up template (I'll paste into meeting notes):
- Action: [short description] | Owner: [name] | Due: [YY-MM-DD HH:MM PT] | Blockers: [if any] | Link: [artifact]

Stuff I need to tidy up after the sync:
- Consolidate action items into JIRA (I usually create RT tickets under JIRA-RT-xxxx).
- Update the public release train doc with final canary image and decisions.
- If any rollback needed, write the chronological timeline and pin to the incident.

Personal reminders:
- Bring up the older safety net doc — has the team validated the traffic shaping thresholds for the new model?
- If time, ask Rowan to annotate the migration plan with explicit pre/post checks (I want checklists, not paragraphs).

Unresolved questions to raise live (these are short):
- Who owns the edge-cache invalidation for feature X? (not in release doc)
- Is there a quick way to disable telemetry for the canary if ingest spikes?
- Confirm that the canary has an SLI baseline for p95 latency (ask SRE to show numbers)

End-of-meeting quick script (what I will say out loud to close):
"Ok — summary: build artifact OK / migrations [status] / canary smoke [status]. Actions: Samir -> promote tag, Rowan -> confirm migration logs, QA -> mark flaky tests + ticket. If anything deviates during the next 2 hours we pause and reconvene. Owners, please update your tickets and post links to this thread."

Last minute: double-check timezones before pinging oncall (PT -> CET overlap).

-- Ava

(End of scratchpad)
